cards.title: Introduction to Java Debugging
cards.content:
Debugging is the systematic process of locating and resolving bugs in your Java application. At its core, the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) supports debugging natively through the JVM Tool Interface (JVMTI).

Two critical concepts to understand are:

  • JDWP (Java Debug Wire Protocol): The protocol used for communication between the debugger (your IDE) and the target JVM.
  • JDI (Java Debug Interface): The high-level Java API used by IDEs to implement debugger features.

cards.title: Analyzing Java Stack Traces
cards.content:
When an unhandled exception occurs, Java prints a stack trace. Learning to read it from bottom to top, and identifying the line originating in your own code package is essential.

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "String.length()" because "str" is null
    at com.example.App.process(App.java:12)
    at com.example.App.main(App.java:8)

In this example, the exception was thrown inside App.java at line 12 inside the process method, which was invoked by the main method at line 8.

cards.title: Stepping Controls in Java Debuggers
cards.content:
When paused at a breakpoint, you have several options to advance execution control:

  • Step Over (F8): Executes the current line of code and moves to the next line in the same file without stepping inside called methods.
  • Step Into (F7): Steps inside the method call present on the current line.
  • Step Out (Shift+F8): Completes execution of the current method and returns you to the calling method context.
  • Drop Frame: Rolls back execution to the beginning of the current stack frame (re-evaluating local states, though it cannot reverse external side-effects like database writes).

cards.title: Dynamic Expression Evaluation
cards.content:
Modern IDEs like IntelliJ IDEA and Eclipse allow you to evaluate arbitrary Java expressions on the fly while execution is suspended.

Watchpoints: You can set watchpoints on instance variables. The debugger will suspend execution whenever the value of that specific variable changes or is read, regardless of which line of code performed the operation.
